question.worked_solution:
The formula for the Newton-Raphson method is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-\frac{f({x}_{n})}{{f}^{′}({x}_{n})}
$$

where ${f}^{′}({x}_{n})$ is the derivative of $f(x)$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=({x}^{4}-2x-1)^{′}=4{x}^{3}-2.
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{n+1} & ={x}_{n}-\frac{{x}^{4}-2x-1}{4{x}_{n}^{3}-2} \\  & =\frac{{x}_{n}(4{x}_{n}^{3}-2)-({x}_{n}^{4}-2{x}_{n}-1)}{4{x}_{n}^{3}-2} \\  & =\frac{3{x}_{n}^{4}+1}{4{x}_{n}^{3}-2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=1.5,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\frac{3{x}_{0}^{4}+1}{4{x}_{0}^{3}-2} \\  & =\frac{3(1.5)^{4}+1}{4(1.5)^{3}-2} \\  & =1.407\,608…\end{aligned}
$$

For the second iteration, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\frac{3{x}_{1}^{4}-1}{4{x}_{1}^{3}-2} \\  & =\frac{3(1.407\,608…)^{4}-1}{4(1.407\,608…)^{3}-2} \\  & ≈1.396,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.
